content: The medication rifabutin is indicated for the prevention of disseminated Mycobacterium avium complex (MAC) disease in patients with advanced HIV infection. The standard dosage is 300 mg orally once daily. If patients experience nausea, vomiting, or gastrointestinal upset, the dose can be adjusted to 150 mg orally twice daily with food. For treatment of MAC disease, the recommended dose is 5 mg/kg orally once daily or 2-3 times per week in combination with other antitubercular agents, not exceeding 300 mg per dose. Rifabutin has orphan designation for the treatment of disseminated MAC disease and pediatric Crohn’s disease when used in combination with clarithromycin, rifabutin, and clofazimine. Rifabutin interacts with numerous medications by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism, leading to decreased levels or effects of these drugs. These interactions often result in contraindications or the need to avoid coadministration. Below are specific examples of these interactions: 1. Apixaban: Rifabutin reduces apixaban levels and anticoagulant effects. Coadministration is contraindicated. 2. Artemether/lumefantrine: Rifabutin decreases their levels, reducing antimalarial efficacy. Coadministration is contraindicated. 3. Cabotegravir: Rifabutin increases cabotegravir metabolism, reducing its effectiveness. Coadministration is contraindicated with extended-release injectable formulations (Cabenuva). 4. Cariprazine: Rifabutin reduces cariprazine levels, and coadministration is contraindicated. 5. Cobicistat: Rifabutin decreases cobicistat levels, reducing its efficacy. Avoid coadministration. 6. Dienogest/estradiol valerate: Rifabutin reduces contraceptive efficacy. Women should avoid using this combination and switch to nonhormonal contraceptives for at least 28 days after discontinuing rifabutin. 7. Doravirine: Rifabutin reduces doravirine levels. If coadministered, increase doravirine dose to 100 mg twice daily. 8. Elbasvir/grazoprevir: Rifabutin reduces their therapeutic effects. Coadministration is contraindicated. 9. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF: Rifabutin decreases their levels, risking virologic failure. Coadministration is contraindicated. 10. Isavuconazonium sulfate: Rifabutin reduces its levels. Coadministration is contraindicated. 11. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir: Rifabutin reduces sofosbuvir levels, decreasing its active metabolite. Coadministration is contraindicated. 12. Lonafarnib: Rifabutin reduces lonafarnib levels. Coadministration is contraindicated. 13. Lorlatinib: Rifabutin reduces lorlatinib levels. Coadministration is contraindicated. 14. Lumacaftor/ivacaftor: Avoid coadministration. 15. Lurasidone: Rifabutin reduces lurasidone levels. Coadministration is contraindicated. 16.
